THIS_IS_NOT_A_CONFORMANCE_VECTOR: Read this before using anything in this file. These values are NOT a reference another implementation can be checked against, and this file deliberately lives outside test_data/vectors/ for that reason.
description: Regression pin on the arithmetic of atl_core::compute_genesis_leaf_hash. It fixes what the function computes today so that a change to it cannot pass unnoticed. That is all it does.

why_it_is_separated.no_first_source: The domain string "ATL-CHAIN-v1", the composition SHA256(0x00 || domain || prev_root_hash || prev_tree_size), and the little-endian encoding of the size appear nowhere in atl-protocol-ietf.md. compute_genesis_leaf_hash and GENESIS_DOMAIN are public API of atl-core, but no specification defines what they are supposed to be.
why_it_is_separated.why_that_disqualifies_it: Every other vector in this repository is checkable against something outside atl-core: an RFC's own text, a published reference set, or a named specification clause plus a formula. This one is not. Its formula was transcribed from the atl-core doc comment, so an independent SHA-256 confirms the ARITHMETIC but nothing confirms the CONTRACT. A third-party implementer has no document to implement it from, and matching these hashes would only mean they copied atl-core.
why_it_is_separated.why_it_is_kept_anyway: A pin that says plainly what it is still catches an accidental change to a public function. What it must never do is sit in test_data/vectors/ where a reader looking for an external reference would take it for one -- that is the same failure as the "root": "computed" placeholders this vector work replaced, merely labelled more honestly.
why_it_is_separated.how_to_promote_it: Either the construction goes into the protocol specification, after which these values can be re-derived from the spec clause and moved into test_data/vectors/atl/, or the API is marked non-protocol in its own doc comment and this file stays where it is.
